name: chest-voice-literal
style: 1997 New York boom bap, 90 BPM, East Coast hardcore hip hop. Male rap vocal: heavyset Brooklyn man in his mid-twenties, deep chest voice, plummy and wheezy, humid breathy tone, thick laid-back grumble with a slight rasp, audible breaths between lines. Calm, unhurried, menacing without raising his voice, every syllable enunciated, sitting right on the beat. Beat: hard dry kick, cracking snare, sparse swung drums, a short dark jazz-piano chord stab looping, vinyl crackle and tape hiss, mono-ish dusty mix, vocal loud and upfront. Between each rule a turntable scratch cuts in a shouted man's voice calling the number. Dark, cold, minimal.
exclude: singing, melodic chorus, autotune, trap hi-hats, 808 bass, synth pads, choir, female vocals, fast double-time flow, shouting rapper, modern polished mix, reverb wash, guitar
lyrics:
[Intro: spoken, low and calm]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Scratch: shouted number cut on the turntable]
[Verse: deep chest voice, unhurried, on the beat]
Number one: never tell 'em what you printed,
trillions out the back door, keep the ledger tinted.

[Scratch: shouted number]
Number two: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Scratch: shouted number]
Number three: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout on tick and they ain't paid at all.

[Outro: spoken, slow, beat drops out]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[End]

name: drums-first-dj-cuts
style: 1997 East Coast boom bap, producer-led. Chopped breakbeat drums sliced and re-stacked on an MPC, kick and snare harder than nails, dry knock, slight swing, 92 BPM. Minimal two-bar loop of dark minor Rhodes chords, sparse and ominous, never resolving. Deep round sub bass walking under the loop. Turntablist cuts the spoken numbers on vinyl between each rule like a radio countdown, sharp chirp scratches. Mono-leaning 90s mix, gritty 12-bit sampler crunch, tape hiss, no chorus. Vocal: big heavyset deep male Brooklyn rapper, chesty and slightly wheezy, slow, cool, conversational, behind the beat, unhurried authority.

A DJ scratches a loud booming announcer voice shouting each number, one cut per number, landing on beat one, stuttered and chopped. Heavy thumping kick, cracking dry snare on two and four, faint shaker, a single ominous low piano chord struck once a bar and left to ring, round sub bass, wide silences between hits. Solo male rapper, heavyset Brooklyn voice: deep, thick, raspy, nasal edge, lazy confident drawl, calm menace with a grin, talks the rules like a big brother laying it out at the table, every syllable clear, words dragged late against the snare, vocal tight and in your ear, dry

name: mafioso-menace

Beat: grimy New York street-corner hip hop from a dusty sampler, a lone eerie Rhodes-style minor-key jazz chord phrase repeating, fat thudding kick, snare that cracks like a slammed door, closed hats, deep upright bass notes, hiss and crackle, saturated cassette warmth, narrow mono mix, vocal dry, close and loud. Each number is a turntable scratch of a gruff barked count. Rules only: no hook, no chorus, no singing.
